q: The notion of algorithmic randomness and unpredictability in chaotic systems is formalized by the result that the Bernoulli shift on k symbols preserves the property that a sequence x ∈ {0,…,k-1}^ω is Martin-Löf random iff:
opts: x has equal frequency of all symbols
K(x₁…xₙ) ≥ n log k − O(1) (incompressible in base k)
exp: Martin-Löf random sequences in {0,…,k-1}^ω are characterised by K(xₙ) ≥ n log k − O(1)—maximal complexity (incompressible). Under the Bernoulli measure (fair k-sided coin), Lebesgue-a.e. sequence is Martin-Löf random, connecting measure theory to algorithmic randomness.
